text:
maya: heads up — canary for the dynamic eager-flush batcher finished. TL;DR: p50 token latency down ~18%, p95 down ~16%, cost/token down ~12%. sharing quick notes and next steps. :tada:
samir: nice!! can you paste the numbers?
maya: metrics from 1h canary vs baseline:
```
metric                baseline      canary    delta
p50 token latency     42.1 ms       34.5 ms   -18.1%
p95 token latency     210.4 ms      175.0 ms  -16.8%
throughput (tokens/s)  9.1k         10.0k     +9.9%
GPU util (avg)         74%          68%       -6 pp
cost / 1M tokens      $3.40        $3.00     -11.8%
kv cache hit rate      71.2%        76.1%     +4.9 pp
```
jin: kv hit rate up is interesting — is that from earlier flushes reducing duplicate prefix work?
maya: exactly. eager flush merges prefixes more aggressively, so the KV cache serves more downstream requests. also reduced wasted decoding for short tail requests.
leo: what about memory/OOMs? any regressions on large-context runs?
maya: we ran 4 stress passes up to 32k context, no OOMs. memory usage slightly higher on host-side (serializer buffer + transient copy) but within slack. no swap observed.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployed dyn-eager-flush v2 -> 09:01 UTC (shard set: sg-3, euw-1)
rachel: outstanding — what's the rollout plan and guardrails?
maya: ramp plan: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over 48h if p95 < 220ms and error rate < 0.05%. automatic rollback to hybrid-batcher if p95 breach persists for 5m. alerting dashboards created: perf / errors / nv-saturations.
ton y: (typo fixed) tony: add a regression fail-open: if any region sees >10% increase in tail latency, immediately route region traffic to fallback model variant.
maya: done. added region-aware policy and a canary runbook.
samir: any anomalies during the run?
maya: small spike in CPU on the host-side serializer for sub-20-token requests around +2m mark — caused brief p50 jitter (+5ms). PR to micro-optimize serializer queued: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4723
jin: cool. schedule a perf sync? would be good to review kernel selection impact and whether eager flush hurts some attention patterns.
maya: yes — perf sync tomorrow 11:00 PT. I'll upload raw traces and perf flamegraphs to the dashboard.
ops-bot: incident-bot: note created (perf-note-1769123456) for canary observations
rachel: this is a big win for Dedicated customers — can you draft a short blurb for product-announcements after 24h stable?
maya: on it. draft will include numbers, recommended knob defaults, and rollout notes.
leo: thanks everyone — great cross-team work. :rocket:
